/* ===== HERO — THE PHOTO'S OWN LIGHTS, ALIVE (Taylor's correction) =====
   The previous build laid generic violet/pink/gold beams + light pools
   OVER the photo — an add-on, not the photo's lights. Those are gone.
   This is the SAME hero photo stacked exactly on itself (same file, same
   box, same object-fit, same sway wrapper, and the camera JS mirrors its
   dolly transform onto this copy every frame, so the two stay registered
   pixel-for-pixel at every viewport and scroll position). The copy is
   contrast-crushed and screen-blended: dark pixels crush to black, and
   screen-blending with black changes nothing — so the crowd, sky and
   shadows are mathematically untouched. Only pixels that are ALREADY
   bright in the photo — the top-truss spots, the purple tower beam on
   the left, the warm stage beams, the footlights, the right-tower
   spots, the LED wall's own glow — lift toward white as the copy's
   opacity/filter breathe slowly. No new beam, no new glow, nothing
   appears where the photo has no light. A luminance mask from the same
   photo (where supported) concentrates the lift further onto those
   same bright areas; where a browser falls back to the photo's alpha
   (fully opaque) the mask is a no-op and the contrast/screen math
   still governs, so it can never become a whole-photo wash.
   Slight and smooth: one slow 5.6s breath, never a flash.
   pointer-events:none keeps Book Now + Gallery tappable.
   Reduced motion: the copy is fully off — the steady photo alone. ===== */
.hero-alive{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;object-position:center;pointer-events:none;mix-blend-mode:screen;opacity:.12;filter:brightness(.92) contrast(2.05) saturate(1.3);-webkit-mask-image:url(data:image/webp;base64,);mask-image:url(data:image/webp;base64,);-webkit-mask-size:cover;mask-size:cover;-webkit-mask-position:center;mask-position:center;-webkit-mask-repeat:no-repeat;mask-repeat:no-repeat;mask-mode:luminance;animation:heroLightsAlive 5.6s ease-in-out infinite;will-change:opacity,filter}
@keyframes heroLightsAlive{0%,100%{opacity:.1;filter:brightness(.9) contrast(2.05) saturate(1.28)}50%{opacity:.5;filter:brightness(1.02) contrast(2.2) saturate(1.38)}}
@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.hero-alive{animation:none;opacity:0}}

/* ===== FEEL THE VIBES — video slideshow =====
   One video at a time, smooth snap, no control row — a single subtle
   animated swipe-right hint sits below the track instead. PER-VIDEO
   FRAMES: there is no single fixed frame. Each slide's frame carries
   that video's own natural aspect ratio — the eleven portrait reels
   (640×1138, slides 1/2/3/5/6/7/8/9/10/11/12) get a tall 320/569 frame
   via .vid-frame.tall, and the three wide videos (640×360, slides
   4/13/14 — the DMT one among them) keep the wide 16/9 frame. Because
   each frame's shape IS its video's shape, object-fit:contain is an
   exact edge-to-edge fill: no side bars, no letterbox, no pillarbox,
   no crop, no stretch, no zoom — every video shown whole, exactly as
   shot. On phone widths a tall frame spans the slide's full width; on
   wide screens its width is capped and centred so a portrait reel
   never becomes a two-metre column. The track's height follows the
   CURRENT slide's frame (see fit() in the slideshow script), so a
   wide video never sits in a tall slide's empty space and a tall
   reel is never clipped by a wide slide's height. The edge-fade
   overlay is OFF for these frames: with the video filling the frame
   exactly, a fade would only wash the picture's own edges.
   Each frame carries the blue neon glow border. Tap a video to play
   it with sound, tap again to pause; the small centre pill is
   pointer-events:none (never a big overlay), and each slide's
   speaker button stays visible as its only mute control. */
